The reverse mode is implemented and verified end to end.

## What I found

A 9-agent audit of the codebase (333 findings) showed the reverse mode wasn't *missing* — it was **half-applied**. Earlier work had swapped the *text* almost everywhere, but the *learner aids, prompt contracts, defaults, and interface strings* attached to that text had not moved with it.

## What I changed

**Prompts** — The explanation contract literally said *"All pinyin fields must be empty strings because the headword is English."* A Mandarin speaker got an English word with no way to pronounce it, while an English speaker got tone-marked pinyin. Worse, [the check runner asserted that defect](scripts/ai-prompt-checks/AIExplanationPromptChecksRunner.swift:100), locking it in. The `pinyin` slot is now the *pronunciation* slot: pinyin for Chinese, **IPA with primary stress** (`/kəˈmɪt/`) for English — across the teacher contract, both JSON schemas, and every `@Guide`. The English word-building contract now mirrors the Chinese one line for line instead of being five prohibitive lines. [`WordIdentificationService`](SwiftMandarin/Services/WordIdentificationService.swift) is direction-parameterized: English segmentation keeps phrasal verbs whole (the mirror of keeping 学习 intact) and glosses in 中文.

**Vocabulary list** — English headword in the main font, 中文 beneath, sized by script so both directions look equally weighted. An English pronunciation line appears where pinyin doesn't apply, guarded by `looksLikeIPA` so a term saved while learning Mandarin can't render "xuéxí" under "study".

**Reader** — [`TranslateView`](SwiftMandarin/Views/TranslateView.swift) rendered `RubyTextView` unconditionally under a hard-coded `"CHINESE (TAP WORDS FOR DETAILS)"`. It now picks the tappable pane by direction; `EnglishRubyTextView` already existed and was simply never wired here.

**Interface language** — ~155 strings never reached the catalog; 149 zh-Hans translations added, coverage **1289/1300** (the rest is punctuation).

## The bug the verification pass caught

Adversarial review found something that would have quietly undone most of the localization work. `LocalizationManager` switches language by re-classing `Bundle.main`. SwiftUI's `Text` goes through that override — **`String(localized:)` does not.** I verified it rather than taking it on trust:

```
Bundle.main.localizedString : 陈述句      ← honored
String(localized:)          : Declarative ← BYPASSED
```

Pre-existing app-wide (~184 sites), but my pass added ~110 more and *documented them as following the toggle*, which was false. All **294** sites now pass `bundle: .appLanguage`, with two mutation-tested guards so it can't regress. Review also caught a genuine build error my bulk rewrite introduced in `SRSEngine` (`comment:` before `bundle:`).

## Verification

`init.sh` is green — 456 assertions including a new 36-assertion mirror suite. I couldn't run `xcodebuild` (no Xcode), but recovered both things it provides: the Ollama package from Xcode's own resolved checkout, plus the project's real build settings. **All 112 files including every SwiftUI view body type-check with zero errors.**

Two things to flag: the iOS-only `#if os(iOS)` regions can't be compiled here (no iOS SDK) — read by hand, but build iOS Debug first. And the IPA contract is asserted against the rendered prompt, not a live model. Recorded in [handoff.md](handoff.md) as Iteration 29.

Fixed and pushed — `ad848f2` on main, in sync.

**Both errors were mine, from the previous commit:**

`AppPreferences.init` seeded `defaultDirection` by reading `self.learnerMode`, which is a `self` access before every stored property is initialized. The resolved mode now lives in a local. `LanguageBundleOverride`'s members were implicitly main-actor-isolated under `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor`, while `appLanguage` is `nonisolated` and `localizedString(forKey:value:table:)` overrides a nonisolated ObjC method — every member of that extension is now explicitly `nonisolated`, which is what it always needed given it's called from `String(localized:bundle:)` throughout the models and services.

**I have to correct something I told you earlier.** I said the app "type-checks with zero errors, all views included" and that Xcode wasn't installed. Both were wrong, and the second caused the first — **Xcode is at `/Applications/Xcode-beta.app`**; only `xcode-select` points at Command Line Tools, and the repo's own check scripts have had that path as their `DEVELOPER_DIR` default the whole time. I should have tried it.

I didn't just patch and re-assert: I reverted both fixes and re-ran my harness, and it still reported clean. So the harness was demonstrably untrustworthy, not merely unlucky. `swiftc -typecheck` skips SIL diagnostic passes and never loads the macro plugins — and `@Observable`'s expansion is precisely what makes `learnerMode` a *computed* access, which is the error. Both facts are now in [handoff.md](handoff.md) so the next session doesn't repeat it.

**Verified with the real compiler:**

```
xcodebuild -scheme SwiftMandarin -destination 'platform=macOS'                  → ** BUILD SUCCEEDED **
xcodebuild -scheme SwiftMandarin -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator'  → ** BUILD SUCCEEDED **
```

Zero errors, zero warnings on both. `init.sh` green at 456 assertions. That also closes the iOS gap I'd flagged as unverified.

**On the "Skipping duplicate build file" warnings** — not caused by my code. `SwiftMandarin/` is a `fileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup`, so everything under it is included automatically, but the project file *also* carries explicit `PBXBuildFile` entries for many of those paths — up to 17 for `StatsView.swift`. Xcode added two more (for `AppPreferences.swift` and `LanguageBundleOverride.swift`) during my first build; I reverted those, and the rebuild went to **0 duplicate warnings on macOS, 1 on iOS** — the remaining one is a pre-existing entry for `AudioSessionCoordinator.swift`.

Deleting every explicit entry for a path under `SwiftMandarin/` would clear it and is verifiable by rebuilding both platforms, but it's project-file surgery unrelated to this work, so I left it and wrote it up as a follow-up. Say the word if you want it done.

**Release:** [v4.2.0](https://github.com/linroger/SwiftMandarin/releases/tag/v4.2.0) — published, not a draft, with the 5.5 MB DMG and its `.sha256`. Notes lead with the two-direction comparison table and list what changed.

**READMEs** — both now describe the app as genuinely two-directional. The English one was still headed *"Your Complete Mandarin Chinese Learning Companion"* with a Mandarin-learner-only overview; the Chinese one had already moved on, so I brought English up to match rather than the reverse. Both gained a **Two Learning Directions** section with a side-by-side table (headline word, pinyin vs IPA, explanation language, which pane is tappable, narration order, tone drills hidden), and the Settings list now says the learner mode re-orients the whole app.

**Versions unified at 4.2.** They were three different numbers — app `3.0`, tag `v4.1.0`, DMG `2.0`. Now `MARKETING_VERSION = 4.2`, `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 42`, DMG named to match.

Two things worth flagging:

I caught a bad DMG before it shipped. The first one came out at **671 KB** for a 19 MB app — an earlier `cp -R` had been killed by a command timeout, leaving a truncated bundle that still packaged without error. I re-staged with `ditto`, and verified the real one by mounting it, copying the app out, and launching it. Had I trusted the exit code, that broken image would be on the release page now.

I also corrected myself mid-edit: I'd written that a native Mandarin reader "sees the phonetics settings instead" of the pinyin controls. That isn't true — I hid the pinyin controls and never built a phonetics section. The line now says plainly there's nothing to configure there.

`main` is at `6aaf9ad`, in sync with the remote, and `init.sh` is green at 456 assertions. The unsigned DMG will still trip Gatekeeper — the right-click → Open note is already in both READMEs and the release notes.

The rest was re-ordering: the 89 keys my script appended to the end got filed into Xcode's collation order. Committed as `c290b39` and pushed.
